events.title: Asian Shares Mixed In Cautious Trade
events.description: Asian stocks turned in a mixed performance on Monday, with AI spending concerns and elevated oil prices keeping investors on edge.

events.title: Euro Slides Against Majors
events.description: The euro weakened against other major currencies in the early European session on Monday.

events.title: European Shares Seen Lower As Violence Erupts At France Protests
events.description: European stocks are seen opening lower on Monday as mass protests in France spiraled into riots, compounding an already elevated fiscal risk premium.

events.title: Indian Shares Modestly Lower In Cautious Trade
events.description: Indian shares were modestly lower in early trade on Monday on concerns over elevated oil prices amid escalating tensions in the Strait of Hormuz.

events.title: Australian Market Maintains Early Gains In Mid-market
events.description: The Australian stock market is maintaining its early gains in mid-market trading on Monday, extending the gains in the previous session, despite the broadly negative cues from Wall Street on Friday. The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 index is moving above the 8,800.00 level, with gains in energy and financial stocks partially offset by weakness in gold miners and technology stocks.

events.title: Asian Markets Track Wall Street Lower
events.description: Asian stock markets are mostly lower on Monday, following the broadly negative cues from Wall Street on Friday, amid spiking crude oil prices as well as a sell-off in technology and semiconductor stocks on concerns of returns on huge AI infrastructure spending. Escalating Middle East tensions and attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz kept oil-supply disruption risks in focus.

events.title: Indian Shares Set For Muted Opening
events.description: Indian shares are seen opening little changed on Monday, tracking mixed cues from global markets.

events.title: Thai Shares Tipped To Open In The Red On Monday
events.description: Ahead of Friday's market holiday, the Thai stock market had alternated between positive and negative finishes through the last five trading days since the end of the five-day winning streak in which it had gained almost 25 points or 1.6 percent. The Stock Exchange of Thailand now sits just beneath the 1,575-point plateau and the losses may accelerate on Monday.

events.title: Japanese Market Sharply Lower
events.description: The Japanese stock market is sharply lower on Monday, reversing some of the gains in the previous session, following the broadly negative cues from Wall Street on Friday. The Nikkei 225 is falling below the 64,450 level, with weakness across most sectors led by index heavyweights and technology stocks.

events.title: Savaged Indonesia Stock Market May Open Lower Again On Monday
events.description: The Indonesia stock market has finished lower in two straight sessions, cratering more than 760 points or 13 percent in that span. The Jakarta Composite Index now sits just above the 5,185-point plateau and it's got a negative lead again for Monday's trade.

events.title: Australian Markets Modestly Higher
events.description: The Australian stock market is modestly higher on Monday, extending the gains in the previous session, despite the broadly negative cues from Wall Street on Friday. The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 index is moving above the 8,800.00 level, with gains in energy and financial stocks partially offset by weakness in gold miners and technology stocks.

events.title: Soft Start Anticipated For China Stock Market
events.description: The China stock market on Friday ended the two-day losing streak in which it had stumbled almost 100 points or 3.2 percent. The Shanghai Composite Index now sits just above the 3,715-point plateau although it may hand those gains back on Monday.

events.title: Taiwan Stock Market May Open Under Water On Monday
events.description: The Taiwan stock market has finished higher in two of three trading days since the end of the four-day losing streak in which it had dropped almost 1,500 points or 3.1 percent. The Taiwan Stock Exchange now sits just above the 47,110-point plateau although it may recede again on Monday.
